# Whether a ball contains another, one-limb center

Kernel `ball_contains_ball_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

Whether $Y \subseteq X$, every member of $Y$ a member of $X$, $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies Y \subseteq X.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when $Y \subseteq X$, every member of $Y$ a member of $X$: the answer is exact.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked. The [Proofs](../proofs/index.md#what-is-proved-and-in-which-model) page says which statements of the IEEE model are proved against statements written by hand; this page gives the status that `gen/claims.json` gives.

## Source

**Algorithm:** the distance of the centers and the difference of the radii as exact pairs, compared (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_contains_ball_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_contains_ball_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum_ord`](two_sum_ord.md), [`abs_2`](abs_2.md), [`le_2_2`](le_2_2.md).

```
# Whether a ball with a one-limb center contains another, Y inside X (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", the row of contains(Y), "Exact pairs"): |c_y - c_x| <= r_x - r_y, decided exactly as
# le_2_2(abs_2(two_sum_ord(c_y, -c_x)), two_sum_ord(r_x, -r_y)). A difference of the centers that
# overflows exceeds every radius. The special states, by the table of "The empty set and the whole
# line": the whole line contains every ball, and the empty set is in every ball; the comparison
# gives false for an empty X and a nonempty Y, and for a whole line Y in a finite X (r_x - inf is
# -inf). Exact.

ncx      = neg(cx)
(d0, d1) = two_sum_ord(cy, ncx)
(a0, a1) = abs_2(d0, d1)
nry      = neg(ry)
(g0, g1) = two_sum_ord(rx, nry)
f        = le_2_2(a0, a1, g0, g1)
wx       = eq(rx, const inf)
qy       = eq(ry, ry)
ey       = not(qy)
sp       = or(wx, ey)
m        = or(sp, f)
```
